newsitem.title: USA: US property & casualty Q3 net dips -industry group.
newsitem.headline: US property & casualty Q3 net dips -industry group.

text.p: The U.S. property & casualty insurance industry's third quarter net income fell to $5.1 billion from $5.8 billion a year ago, according to figures released by the Insurance Services Office Inc (ISO) and the National Association of Independent Insurers (NAII).
The figures are consolidated estimates for the entire industry based on the reports of insurers that account for 96 percent of the country's property/casualty insurance business.

Net income for the third quarter 1996 consisted of $1.0 billion in realized capital gains and operating income of $5.3 billion. The industry paid $1.2 billion in income taxes in the third quarter, compared with $1.5 billion in third quarter 1995.
For the first nine months of the year, the industry's consolidated net income rose to $16.8 billion from $15.1 billion a year earlier.
Net income in this year's first nine months included $18.8 billion of operating income and $6.9 billion of realized gains, according to the industry groups.
The industry paid $3.9 billion in income taxes, a decrease of 4.7 percent from the $4.0 billion in the first nine months of 1995.
